title: Comparative study on thermal performance of Fe3O4 ferrofluids with cylindrical and spherical nanoparticles: Chain‐like structure and heat transfer characteristics
content:
Abstract

Based on the analogy approach between permittivity and thermal conductivity, an equation was derived to consider the effect of spherical and cylindrical magnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles shape factor on the effective thermal conductivity of a Fe3O4 ferrofluid caused by chain-like structure (FHD effect). Following this, a comparative study was done between the thermal performance of Fe3O4 ferrofluids, containing spherical and cylindrical Fe3O4 magnetic nanoparticles, when flowed as a hot flow in a mini channel under different magnetic field intensities, nanoparticles concentration and flow conditions. Finally, RSM optimization was recruited to investigate the optimum conditions. The results revealed that cylindrical shape Fe3O4 magnetic nanoparticles can form chain-like structure easier than spherical nanoparticles. Consequently, cylindrical magnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles enhance the effective thermal conductivity of ferrofluid more than spherical shape nanoparticles do. Also, for both nanoparticle shapes there is a saturation magnetic field for FHD effect such that as the magnetic field intensity increases, the effective thermal conductivity of ferrofluid initially rises sharply to a maximum value and then remains almost constant. For both nanoparticle shapes an increase in nanoparticle concentration raises the effective thermal conductivity. However, in a fixed concentration of nanoparticles, cylindrical shape nanoparticles have a higher impact on the enhancement of effective thermal conductivity than spherical shape. Finally, comparison of the overall heat transfer coefficients (OHTC) in a mini-channel with Fe3O4–water ferrofluid as the hot flow indicates that the magnetic field enhances OHTC for both spherical and cylindrical Fe3O4 nanoparticles, with a greater effect observed for the cylindrical shape.
